text:
Maya: heads-up @channel — notify-orch is suppressing pages for ~5m, oncall didn't get any pages. Customers pinged ops. Looks like autoclear/squelch is toggling rapidly :thinking:
IncidentBot: alert: suppressed 42 events from notify-orch in last 300s (policy=autoclear)
Cheng: looking...
Alex: can someone check incidentbot queue and notify webhook headers? suspect TTL/units mismatch between notify-orch and incidentbot
Maya: quick log snippet showing the pattern:
```
2026-03-18T09:12:43Z notify-orch: event_id=abc123 action=send status=200 squelch=true ttl=0
2026-03-18T09:12:44Z incidentbot: enqueue=0 dropped=1 reason=autoclear ttl_ms=0
```
Cheng: TTL=0 stands out. There's a config-regen cron that writes ttl; maybe wrote 0 instead of 30s after a change.
Alex: FYI incidentbot v2.4 treats ttl<=0 as 'squelch immediately' (regression). That explains no pages.
SRE-Ops: I can force pages while we fix; will run manual page for affected events.
Maya: doing manual pages to the impacted customers now, pinging current on-call (@alex).
SRE-Ops: manual command used: `/ops force-page team=oncall reason="autoclear bypass" event_ids=abc123,def456`
DeployBot: config-regen job (service=deploy/config-regen, image=sha256:ef12) finished at 09:10 UTC
Cheng: rolling back config-regen to previous image and preparing patch to ensure ttl is written in seconds (int) and never 0. Will redeploy in ~5m.
Maya: temporary mitigation: add a guard in incidentbot to treat ttl<1 as TTL=30s (hotfix PR: https://git.internal/redwood/incidentbot/pull/234)
Alex: posting status update to status.redwood.ai and notifying support leads. Customer comms queued.
SRE-Ops: after rollback+hotfix I see squelch counters dropping — monitor snapshot:
```
09:18:00 squelch=12
09:19:00 squelch=2
09:20:00 squelch=0
```
Maya: on-call confirmed they received pages at 09:20 :thumbsup:
Cheng: root cause summary: config-regen wrote TTL as 0 due to integer parse error when REQUIRED env var was missing; incidentbot interpreted <=0 as immediate suppression. Fixes: default ttl=30s, validate config schema, add unit + e2e tests.
Alex: postmortem owners: Cheng (tech lead), Maya (comms). I'll start the customer impact doc.
Maya: I'll open the retro doc and timeline (/docs/incidents/1744444444-retro). Immediate actions: revert config-regen change, release incidentbot hotfix, add schema validation in config-regen. Impact: 4 customers affected, 3 required manual pages.
IncidentBot: system: escalation automation resumed
Maya: closing the live thread; will circulate the postmortem draft in #incidents and ping leadership.
